title: Make Your Team Stronger: Analysis on Network and Team Performance

section_map.summary: Abstract: context-framing via development-direction calque, method preview (two models), result preview (TAI+correlation), suggestions + generalization.
Table of contents listing all sections and page numbers.
Problem restatement, literature review (8 citations), four-task outline, flow chart.
Soccer as world's largest sport; data era enables accurate assessment; four tasks from competition.
Six author-chain citations covering network analysis, performance indicators, team assembly.
Two models + indicators + sensitivity + suggestions + extension; flow chart Figure 1.
Four assumptions: particle, 2D plane, linear summation, player position.
Table 1: 7 main parameters (GD, TAI, P, H, R1-R4).
Main players by pass count; formation from average positions (5-4-1); network diagram.
Four tactics (BPBC, OPSP, DPOP, LRT) via coordinate inequalities; frequency charts.
Four tactical styles via 15-min possession-position matrix; Games 9 and 15 case studies.
Goal difference (GD) as results-oriented performance measure.
Six factors: Pezzali P, H indicator, R1-R4; AHP for R2; EWM weighting; TAI formula.
SPSS significance 0.024; z-score polygraph; Q-Q diagram verification.
Pezzali and H fluctuation CIs; outlier removal (Game 16); single-factor stability.
Four formation recommendations: 4-3-3 vs 4-4-2, avoid 4-4-2, prefer 5-defender, counter 5-back.
F6 best forward, M13 best midfield, D8 best defender via AHP ability values.

Innovative 15min analysis; three-level network; comprehensive evaluation; practical data.

11 references (with 3 duplicates); spanning network analysis, sports analytics.
AHP judgment matrices (F, M, D with CI values); MATLAB code for AHP and EWM.

contributions.summary: Coordinate-inequality screening for four specific tactical patterns (BPBC, OPSP, DPOP, LRT).
Six-factor composite index (TAI) via entropy weight method with statistical validation.
15-minute tactical style classification into four categories using possession-position matrix.
Position-specific player ability quantification via AHP with consistency checks.
Analogy-based extension from soccer to business/R&D team evaluation.

assumptions.summary: Particle assumption: player as point mass, ball route as simple connection.
Two-dimensional plane: ignore vertical space, analyze horizontal tactics only.
Linear summation: EWM requires linear indicator superposition.
Player position: manager assigns players to appropriate positions only.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: MCM-provided passing event data for Huskies full season; passer, receiver, coordinates, timestamps.
Goal difference computed per game from match results.
Field divided into 10x10 zones for zone-level passing statistics.

models.summary: Multi-level network analysis: macro (formation), micro (4 tactics via inequalities), middle (4 styles via possession-position).
Multi-angle performance evaluation: 6 factors, EWM weighting, TAI composite, SPSS correlation.
Analytic hierarchy process: position-specific player ability (F/M/D weight vectors, CI checks).

verification.summary: SPSS correlation TAI-GD significance 0.024; Q-Q diagram scatter around relationship curve.
Pezzali CI [2.6381,3.9982] at 90%; H CI [2.8962,3.7401] at 90%. Model stable under single-factor fluctuation.
Tactic frequency counts validate micro model: Game 30 (12 tactics, 2-0 win) vs Game 9 (0 tactics, 2-5 defeat).
AHP consistency: CI values 0.1121, 0.0341, 0.0342 all pass threshold.

results_trace.summary: model output: TAI = 0.3575P + 0.0908H + 0.1625R1 + 0.1168R2 + 0.1883R3 + 0.0842R4 → interpretation: Pezzali dominates (35.75%).
model output: significance 0.024 → visual: z-score polygraph + Q-Q diagram → answer: significant positive correlation confirmed.
model output: CIs → interpretation: single-factor fluctuation does not destabilize TAI → answer: model robust.
model output: formation comparison → interpretation: 4-3-3 beats 4-4-2; 5-defender above average → answer: four formation recommendations.
model output: AHP ability values → visual: Figure 15 bar chart → answer: F6, M13, D8 best by position.

weaknesses.summary: Correlation-causation conflation: significance 0.024 does not prove causal mechanism.
Analogy-based generalization without any data or validation for non-soccer domains.
Data limitation prevents detailed pitch-level tactical analysis.
Ignores morale, team identity, and cohesion as performance factors.
Three duplicate references ([2], [9], [11] all cite Cintia et al. 2015).
Formula numbering skips from 5 to 7 — editorial error.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Multi-level passing network confirms network-based team analysis pattern.
SPSS correlation + sensitivity analysis validates composite index.
Standard MCM passing event data preprocessing.
Four explicit bullet assumptions with justifications.

independent_extensions.summary: Coordinate-inequality tactical screening could be extended to other team sports with spatial passing data.
EWM weighting pipeline reusable for any multi-indicator composite index.
15-minute tactical style classification adaptable to other time-windowed strategy analysis.
Position-specific AHP ability model applicable to any role-differentiated team evaluation.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Six-factor EWM composite with statistical validation likely impressed judges as systematic and objective.
Coordinate-inequality tactical screening is creative and directly interpretable.
Confidence interval sensitivity analysis demonstrates rigor beyond basic papers.
